concepts.title: Index Numbers: Barometers of Economic Activity

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Index Numbers: Barometers of Economic Activity' refers to.
questions.a: An index number is a statistical device for measuring changes in a variable -- or a group of related variables -- over time or place, expressed relative to a base period taken as 100. Called the barometers of economic activity, index numbers gauge price levels, industrial output and business conditions at a glance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Index Numbers: Barometers of Economic Activity'.
questions.a: One number, one base of 100 -- the index turns sprawling changes into a single readable dial.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Index Numbers: Barometers of Economic Activity' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Price Index: Simple and Weighted Averages

questions.q: Compute the price index using the aggregate expenditure method. Use the method 'Price Index: Simple and Weighted Averages'. Work with: base_price = 1200, current_price = 5000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of price_index.

Find the price relative of each commodity and average them. Use the method 'Price Index: Simple and Weighted Averages'. Work with: base_price = 1200, current_price = 8000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of price_index.
Explain in your own words what 'Price Index: Simple and Weighted Averages' refers to.
questions.a: A simple price index compares a commodity's current price with its base price; aggregate and average-of-relatives methods extend this to many commodities. Weighted index numbers attach importance weights -- typically quantities -- so that items bought in bulk move the index more than rare ones.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Price Index: Simple and Weighted Averages'.
questions.a: Current over base times 100 -- the price index is a ratio dressed as a percentage.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Price Index: Simple and Weighted Averages', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Consumer Price Index and Inflation Measurement

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Consumer Price Index and Inflation Measurement' refers to.
questions.a: The consumer price index tracks the retail prices of a basket of goods and services bought by a typical family, revealing changes in the cost of living; wholesale and industrial-production indices serve other sectors. Real income is nominal income deflated by the price index -- the index that links money to its true worth.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Consumer Price Index and Inflation Measurement'.
questions.a: The CPI is the cost-of-living dial -- divide money income by the index to know real worth.
